title: Phase 0: Specification Documents
description: Create FEATURE-MATRIX.md, docs/PROVENANCE.md, and LICENSE-MATRIX.md before any code. These documents serve as source of truth for algorithm provenance tracking (especially GPL-2.0 jp2a warning), detailed per-function feature matrix, and license compliance. Phase 0 is already partially done (6 repos cloned, audits complete), but these three docs must exist before Phase 1 begins. PROVENANCE.md tracks every algorithm studied: source file, license, whether code was copied or independently rewritten. FEATURE-MATRIX.md maps every function in the 6 reference repos to agent-eye status.
close_reason: Pushed 7c602c8: FEATURE-MATRIX.md, docs/PROVENANCE.md, LICENSE-MATRIX.md. All 6 repos audit-corrected. Companions: LICENSE-MATRIX(chafa split GPL-3/tool vs LGPL-3.0+ lib, jp2a GPL-2.0-only, pixel2ascii no LICENSE file) + PROVENANCE(spec-level ideas only, zero lines copied, matrix append-only).

title: Phase 1: Workspace Setup
description: Set up Rust Cargo workspace with 3 crates: ae-core, ae-render, ae-cli. Create rust-toolchain.toml, rustfmt.toml, clippy.toml. Workspace Cargo.toml defines shared settings. Each crate has its own Cargo.toml with proper dependency declarations. Add CI workflow (GitHub Actions) for fmt + clippy + test on Linux/macOS/Windows. Verify cargo build works.
close_reason: Pushed c1f796f: workspace {ae-core, ae-render, ae-cli(bin ae)}, rust-toolchain(stable), rustfmt+clippy configs, GH Actions matrix CI with fmt/clippy/test/smoke. cargo build/test/clippy/fmt green locally.

title: Phase 1: Canonical Image Representation
description: Define canonical Image + PixelBuffer types in ae-core that do NOT expose image crate types. Image { dimensions: Dimensions, pixels: PixelBuffer, metadata: ImageMetadata }. Pixel { r: u8, g: u8, b: u8, a: u8 }. PixelBuffer is a flat Vec<Pixel>. This abstraction gives freedom to change decoding/storage without infecting the API. Include Dimensions { width: u32, height: u32 } and Bounds types.
close_reason: Pushed: image.rs with Image/PixelBuffer/Pixel/Dimensions/ImageMetadata/Limits. No image-crate types leak. Rec.709 luminance single source of truth. Limits.check_input rejects bombs pre-allocation. 21 tests green.

title: Phase 1: HalfOpenBounds + CoordinateTransform
description: Define HalfOpenBounds { x1, y1, x2, y2 } (inclusive-exclusive) for internal coordinate representation. Expose as [x, y, width, height] at JSON boundary. Define CoordinateTransform { source: HalfOpenBounds, output_width, output_height, scale_x: f64, scale_y: f64, offset_x: f64, offset_y: f64 } with mapping: source_x = output_x * scale_x + offset_x. This is the affine transform foundation for all crop/resize/zoom/region operations.
close_reason: Pushed: geometry.rs HalfOpenBounds (validate/half-open contains/array form) + CoordinateTransform affine (crop=offset-only, resize=scale-only, zoom=both verified by tests). fmt/clippy/test green.

title: Phase 1: Error Types (AeError)
description: Define AeError enum with thiserror: Decode, InvalidDimensions, UnsupportedFormat, ResourceLimit, Rendering, Serialization. Each variant wraps a String message. CLI maps AeError to human-readable stderr output. Library users get structured error types.
close_reason: Pushed: AeError in ae-core/src/error.rs, all 6 plan variants + ctors + Result alias, display-tested; fmt/clippy/test green.

title: Phase 1: Provenance Module
description: First-class Provenance struct in ae-core: Provenance { source_hash: String (sha256), source_bounds: HalfOpenBounds, transform: CoordinateTransform }. Every output includes provenance so agent never loses connection to original image. This is a core product guarantee, not sprinkled throughout commands.
close_reason: Pushed: provenance.rs first-class module. sha256 of original bytes (FIPS vector tested), bounds+transform attached, serde-serializable. 25 tests green.

title: Phase 1: Image Decode (PNG/JPEG/WebP)
description: Implement image decoding using image crate (internal only, not exposed through ae-core API). Support PNG, JPEG, WebP. Decode to canonical Image type. Implement DecodeLimits { max_file_size: 100MB, max_pixels: 25_000_000, max_width: 100_000, max_height: 100_000 }. Check dimensions BEFORE allocating memory (decompression bomb protection). stdin input via '-' argument or piped binary. Golden tests for each format.
close_reason: Pushed: decode.rs decode_bytes(bytes,&Limits)->Image. PNG/JPEG/WebP via magic sniff; dims checked pre-allocation vs Limits; malformed input -> AeError::Decode never panic. In-memory round-trip tests all formats.

title: Phase 1: Security Limits + Decompression Bomb Protection
description: Resource limits enforced at decode time: max_file_size=100MB, max_decoded_pixels=25M, max_width=100K, max_height=100K, max_processing_time=30s. Check decoded dimensions BEFORE allocating pixel buffer. Reject images where width*height > max_pixels. For ZIP-based formats check compressed size ratio. Malformed input → graceful error, never panic. Fuzz testing target.
close_reason: Pushed: Limits+max_processing_time enforced in decode path; bombs rejected pre-allocation by arithmetic; proptest no-panic suite (random/truncated/determinism/consistency). 44 tests green.

title: Phase 1: CI Pipeline
description: GitHub Actions workflow: fmt check, clippy warnings-as-errors, cargo test, cargo bench (baseline). Matrix: ubuntu, macos, windows. Rust stable. Add regression guards: binary size +20% warning, startup time +30% warning.
close_reason: Pushed: GH Actions matrix (linux/macos/windows) fmt+clippy(-D warnings)+test+smoke from nbr; now + guards job (binary size/startup regression vs self-seeding per-OS baseline, ::warning at +20%/+30%) + cargo bench job. Local bench verified.

title: Phase 2: Luminance Engine
description: Implement Rec. 709 luminance calculation: lum = 0.2126*R + 0.7152*G + 0.0722*B. Always computed internally for analysis, not presentation. --grayscale is only a presentation/output mode. No duplicate pipelines. Luminance maps pixel blocks to float [0.0, 255.0] range. Unit tests: pure black→0, pure white→255, known mid-tones.
close_reason: Pushed: analysis.rs luminance engine (Rec.709 0.2126/0.7152/0.0722) as the only luminance pipeline; presentation grayscale stays a separate future flag. Block averaging overflow-safe.

title: Phase 2: Block Sampling + Aspect Correction
description: Block sampling: block_w = img_width / ascii_width, block_h = block_w / aspect_ratio. Default aspect_ratio = 0.5 (terminal chars ~2x tall as wide). --no-aspect → 1.0 (square). Per block: average RGB, compute luminance. Fix ASCII-generator bug: don't hardcode cell_height = 2*cell_width, handle CJK/emoji double-width per charset width class. Unit tests for edge cases: 1x1 image, very wide/narrow, aspect ratios.
close_reason: Pushed: sampling.rs — sample_blocks(img,out_w,out_h,aspect) with block_w=ceil-div, block_h=block_w/aspect (default 0.5, validate finite>0), per-block channel-averaged Pixel + source bounds for provenance; grid capped at image resolution; deterministic. Edge cases covered: 1x1 image, very wide/narrow, aspect variants, zero grid, NaN/inf aspect. 22 render tests green, workspace 66 tests green, clippy+fmt clean. Commit f79392e on master.

title: Phase 2: Charset System
description: Charset { name, glyphs: Vec<char> }. Presets: standard (@%#*+=-:. ), dense (@M#W876543210?...), blocks (█▓▒░ ). Custom charset from CLI --charset flag. Use unicode-segmentation for multi-codepoint emoji (lesson from RASCII). Skip font8x8 intensity computation (dead code in pixel2ascii). brightness-based sorting for charsets (lesson from ASCII-generator). Unit tests: preset counts, custom charset parsing, emoji handling.
close_reason: Pushed: charset.rs — Charset{name,glyphs:Vec<String>}, grapheme splitting via unicode-segmentation (emoji ZWJ safe), presets standard/dense/blocks + resolve(), luminance-to-glyph mapping round+clamp, inverted() view, MAX_CHARSET_LEN=128. 11 unit tests green; clippy+fmt clean. Commit f545624 on master.

title: Phase 2: ASCII Renderer
description: ASCII renderer: for each block, map luminance to charset character. idx = round(lum / 255.0 * (charset_len - 1)). char = charset[idx]. Output: Vec<Vec<char>> grid. Scalar implementation first, parallelize only after profiling. Golden tests: known image → exact ASCII output. Deterministic: same input + same config = identical output every run.
close_reason: Pushed: render.rs — render(img,cfg,charset) shared path; luminance→glyph via Charset; RenderedGrid rows of grapheme strings + to_text(); invert via inverted() charset; render_ascii/render_blocks convenience wrappers; deterministic. 10 renderer tests incl golden 2x1 gradient '@ ' and determinism. Workspace 76 tests green, clippy+fmt clean. Commit e58bb52.

title: Phase 2: Blocks Renderer
description: Unicode blocks renderer using █▓▒░ characters. Same block sampling as ASCII but different charset mapping. Higher spatial density than ASCII. Unit tests, golden tests. Deterministic output.
close_reason: Pushed: same render.rs shared path with blocks preset (█▓▒░ ); RendererKind::Blocks; higher spatial density per cell vs ASCII. Golden tests dark→█ white→space. Commit e58bb52 on master.

title: Phase 2: RenderConfig + RendererType
description: RenderConfig { renderer: RendererType, width: u32, aspect_ratio: f32, invert: bool, charset: Option<String>, color: ColorMode }. RendererType enum: ASCII, Blocks. ColorMode enum: None (agent default), Grayscale, TrueColor. Invert: flip luminance mapping (dark→bright, bright→dark). Unit tests for each config combination.
close_reason: Pushed: config.rs — RenderConfig{renderer,width,aspect_ratio,invert,charset_override,color}, RendererType ascii|blocks with parse/as_str/default_charset, ColorMode none|grayscale|truecolor with v1 support gate (unsupported modes rejected explicitly), validate() enforces aspect finite>0, width 1..=10000 (plan §14), charset resolution preset-or-custom. 9 config tests; workspace 85 green; clippy+fmt clean. Commit 42c89b2 on master.

title: Phase 2: Golden Test Suite
description: Golden test fixtures in tests/fixtures/: simple-box.png, checkerboard.png, gradient.png. For each fixture + each renderer + each config: compute output, compare to stored golden file. If renderer changes, golden diff shows exactly what changed. Determinism tests: run same input 10x, verify identical output.

title: Phase 3: Grayscale Presentation Mode
description: Add --grayscale flag as presentation/output mode only. Analysis luminance is always computed internally. --grayscale outputs grayscale ANSI or plain text. Not the same as the internal luminance computation.

title: Phase 3: Full Terminal Fit
description: Detect terminal size (terminal_size crate). --full flag fits output to terminal width while preserving aspect ratio. Agent default is NOT terminal fit — agent uses explicit --width or default.

title: Phase 3: Stdin Piping
description: Support piped binary input: cat image.png | ae render - . Also support ae render - for explicit stdin. Binary mode on Windows (_setmode). BufReader for performance.

title: Phase 3: Multilingual Charsets
description: Extend charset presets with multilingual options: CJK, Cyrillic, extended ASCII. Lesson from ASCII-generator: support multiple languages with proper font metrics. Use unicode-segmentation for grapheme clusters.

title: Phase 3: File Output
description: Output flag writes result to file instead of stdout. BufWriter for performance. Error if file exists without overwrite flag. stdout remains default for all commands.

title: Phase 3: ae inspect Command
description: ae inspect is orchestrated convenience, NOT a primitive. Internally composes ImageAnalyzer + RegionDetector + RelationEngine + Renderer. Output: dimensions, regions, geometry, rendering, mapping. JSON output with schema_version agent-eye.scene.v1. CLI is orchestration only, business logic lives in ae-core and ae-render.

title: Phase 3: ae render Command
description: ae render with --renderer ascii|blocks. Supports --width, --aspect, --invert, --charset, --format text|json. Two separate axes: renderer (what to render with) and format (how to present output). JSON output with schema_version agent-eye.render.v1.

title: Phase 3: ae capabilities Command
description: ae capabilities --format json outputs schema_version, version, input formats, renderers, commands, output_formats, and limits (max_pixels, max_file_size, max_region_count, max_render_width, max_render_height, max_charset_length). Agent discovers ae capabilities dynamically. Schema: agent-eye.capabilities.v1.

title: Phase 3: JSON Output All Commands
description: All commands support --format json. Versioned schemas: agent-eye.scene.v1, agent-eye.region.v1, agent-eye.geometry.v1, agent-eye.render.v1, agent-eye.capabilities.v1. No semantic labels in JSON. No prohibited fields. Every output includes mapping with CoordinateTransform.

title: Phase 4: Edge Detection
description: Implement edge detection (Sobel or similar) in ae-core analysis module. Input: Image. Output: edge map (Vec of edge strengths per pixel). Scalar implementation first. Unit tests: known gradient → expected edges.

title: Phase 4: Contrast Analysis
description: Compute contrast metrics: local contrast per region, global contrast, dynamic range. Used internally for VisualComplexity. Not exposed in CLI v1.

title: Phase 4: Color Variance Computation
description: Compute color variance per image region. Used for VisualComplexity score. Internal only, not CLI-exposed in v1.

title: Phase 4: VisualComplexity Internal
description: VisualComplexity struct: edge, gradient, variance, redundancy, score (weighted aggregate). Internal implementation detail for future --budget (P1). Not exposed in CLI v1. Purely geometric/statistical, not task-relevant.

title: Phase 5A: Region Contract + Fixtures
description: Define CandidateRegion contract BEFORE implementing. Create test fixtures: ui.png, diagram.png, screenshot.png. Define expected behavior: what regions SHOULD be detected, what should NOT. Write stability measurement tests: same image 10x -> same regions. Document: region is deterministic geometric candidate, NOT semantic interpretation. No guaranteed correspondence to human-perceived layout.

title: Phase 5B: Region Detection Heuristic
description: Implement first heuristic: edge map, whitespace segmentation, connected component analysis, merge overlapping rectangles. CandidateRegion { id, bounds: HalfOpenBounds, area, edge_density, color_variance }. Deterministic sort: y then x then area then stable tie-break. max_region_count: 500.

title: Phase 5C: Region Benchmark
description: Benchmark region quality against fixtures. Measure: detection stability, region count distribution, overlap with human annotations (if available). Critical gate: if regions do not help agent tasks in Phase 7, simplify or remove.

title: Phase 5D: Expose Regions Through Commands
description: Wire CandidateRegion into ae inspect and ae geometry commands. Region IDs appear in JSON output. Relations computed from regions. Provenance includes region bounds.

title: Phase 6: Spatial Relations (7 Core)
description: Implement 7 spatial relations with formal half-open bounds math: left_of(A.x2<=B.x1), right_of, above, below, inside, contains, overlaps. Touching boxes: A.x2==B.x1 means left_of (documented). Deterministic ordering: relation_type then a.id then b.id. max_relation_count bounded by O(n2) x max_region_count.

title: Phase 6: Coordinate Mapping (Affine)
description: Implement CoordinateTransform for all operations. crop changes offset, resize changes scale, zoom changes both. Every output includes transform so agent can map back to original coordinates. Formally: source_x = output_x * scale_x + offset_x.

title: Phase 6: Provenance Tracking
description: Every output includes Provenance { source_hash, source_bounds, transform }. Agent never loses connection to original image. SHA-256 of original image bytes stored in provenance.

title: Phase 6: ae zoom Command
description: ae zoom: crop + resample at specified scale. Levels: 0=1x, 1=2x, 2=4x, 3=8x spatial allocation scale. NOT detail increase — more output samples devoted to smaller source region. Underlying ZoomConfig { scale: f32, output_width: u32 }. Deterministic and predictable. JSON output with provenance.

title: Phase 6: ae region Command
description: ae region extracts specific area with full provenance. Output: source image metadata, region metadata, rendered representation, provenance. JSON schema: agent-eye.region.v1.

title: Phase 6: ae geometry Command
description: ae geometry outputs spatial evidence: all regions, all relations, all coordinates. JSON schema: agent-eye.geometry.v1. Agent uses this for spatial reasoning: left_of, above, inside, etc.

title: Phase 7: Agent Evaluation Harness
description: Build bench/ directory: cases.jsonl, agent-eval.sh, run-case.sh, evaluate scripts, results directory. cases.jsonl format: {id, image, task, type}. Task types: spatial, geometry, counting, detail, structure, progressive, negative. Run modes: baseline (no ae), ascii, blocks, ae-inspect, ae-progressive. Capture: answer, ae_calls, ae_tokens_used, tool_calls, bytes_transferred, duration_ms.

title: Phase 7: 4-Tier Benchmark Implementation
description: Tier 1: Correctness (decode, dimensions, crop, region, zoom, determinism). Tier 2: Representation Quality (spatial preservation, edge preservation, detail preservation, ASCII vs Blocks). Tier 3: Context Efficiency (output bytes, tokens, visual information retained per token). Tier 4: Agent Task Benchmark (spatial, geometry, counting, detail, structure, progressive, negative). Compare: LLM alone, LLM+ASCII, LLM+Blocks, LLM+ae-inspect, LLM+ae-progressive, Vision model upper bound.

title: Phase 7: Negative Capability Test Cases
description: Test cases where ae heuristic evidence is INSUFFICIENT. Correct behavior: agent says I cannot determine from available representation, NOT hallucinated certainty. Tests calibrated uncertainty. Example: tiny button text not readable from representation -> agent should acknowledge limitation.

title: Phase 7: Progressive Inspection Test Cases
description: Test whether targeted zoom resolves uncertainty that overview cannot. Measure: overview sufficient? if no, targeted inspection -> answer. This is the actual hypothesis behind Agent-Eye. Measure task accuracy per unit of context + interaction cost, not just accuracy.

title: Phase 7: Performance Benchmarks
description: Decode time (1MP, 5MP, 10MP, 20MP), render time per renderer (scalar first), region detection per complexity, zoom per crop size, memory peak (RSS), startup time, binary size, dependency count. CI regression guards: binary size +20% warning, startup time +30% warning.

title: Phase 7: PROJECT GATE Decision
description: PROJECT GATE: after Phase 7 benchmark completes, make explicit continue/simplify decision. CONCRETE SUCCESS CRITERIA: (1) ae-progressive mode achieves >=10% higher task accuracy than fixed ASCII at same token budget, OR (2) ae-progressive achieves same accuracy with >=30% fewer tokens. EITHER condition = continue to Phase 8. NEITHER condition = simplify: drop region/zoom/geometry from v1, keep rendering only. Decision must be documented with benchmark numbers. This gate is NON-NEGOTIABLE — plan is a guide, not a contract.

title: Phase 8: Braille Renderer (P1)
description: Braille renderer using Unicode braille patterns U+2800..U+28FF. 2x4 dot cells per character = 8x density vs ASCII. Only implement if Phase 7 benchmark shows value. Floyd-Steinberg dithering for braille (binary dots on/off). --threshold flag for braille dot activation.

title: Phase 8: Dithering (P1)
description: Floyd-Steinberg error diffusion dithering. Only meaningful for braille output (binary dots). Algorithm: reimplement from Go dither/v2. --dither flag. Unit tests: known input -> expected dithered output.

title: Phase 8: ANSI Truecolor Compatibility (P1)
description: ANSI truecolor output via --color flag. Compatibility feature for human terminal display, NOT agent default. Cache last ANSI style to avoid repeating same escape codes (lesson from RASCII: 1800% output reduction on flat-color regions). Use owo-colors or anstyle (replacing unmaintained ansi_term).

title: Phase 8: Adaptive Budget (P1)
description: Only implement if Phase 7 benchmark proves value. --budget N flag. Internal: VisualComplexity drives information density allocation. Agent sees optimized representation within budget. Algorithm: rank regions by complexity, allocate tokens accordingly. NOT implemented before benchmark evidence.

title: Phase 8: Batch Processing (P1)
description: Batch mode: ae inspect ./images/ --format json. Parallel processing with rayon. JSONL output (one JSON object per line). Output naming deterministic.

title: Phase 9: MCP Server (P1)
description: ae-mcp crate. MCP server wrapping core primitives. Tools: inspect_image, render_image, zoom_image, inspect_geometry. No LLM, no HTTP. MCP exposes CLI/core primitives only.

title: Phase 10: Fuzzing + Property Tests
description: Fuzz image decoder (cargo-fuzz), CLI args, JSON schema, region parser. Property tests (proptest): valid image never panics, output dimensions bounded, JSON always valid, determinism, no NaN in coordinates.

title: Phase 10: Cross-Platform CI + Release
description: CI matrix: Linux, macOS, Windows. Release pipeline: crates.io publish, GitHub releases with binaries (x86_64-linux, x86_64-windows, aarch64-macos). rust-toolchain.toml pins stable.

title: Phase 1: Determinism Contract
description: Define and test determinism contract: given identical input bytes, library version, configuration, and platform-independent algorithm parameters, ae produces identical machine-readable output. Region IDs sorted y then x then area then stable tie-break. Relations sorted same way. Parallelism (rayon) must not alter output ordering. Test: run same input 10x, verify byte-identical JSON output. This is a core product guarantee.

title: Phase 8: Background Color (P1)
description: Background color support for rendering (--background flag). P1 feature from compatibility matrix. Only implement after v1 proven per plan.

title: Phase 10: Documentation
description: User docs, library API docs (rustdoc), CLI help text polish, README examples for all v1 commands. Required before release pipeline.
